title: Halloween Kaomoji [¬º-°]¬: Copy & Paste Spooky Text Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste Halloween kaomoji: ghosts like ᗣ, bats /|\ ^._.^ /|\, vampire grins (｀皿´)ψ, zombie walkers [¬º-°]¬, pumpkin faces and witches casting spells.
hero_tagline: Ghosts, bats, vampires, zombies and witches typed out in text, ready for an October caption or a spooky group chat. Tap a face and it is on your clipboard.
intro: Halloween text faces borrow shapes from all over Unicode. The Canadian syllabic ᗣ has a rounded top and a wavy hem, so it reads as a sheet ghost, the same one that chases ᗧ in Pac-Man text art. A bat is a face between two wings made of /|\, and a zombie is a face with one arm stretched forward by ¬. There is no fang character, so vampire faces use 皿, a Japanese character for a dish whose bars look like bared teeth, or the small triangle ▿. Most people post these in the last week of October, up to Halloween night on 31 October. For pictures rather than text, the 🎃 👻 🦇 emoji and themed symbols are on the Halloween symbols page linked below.

sections.label: Ghosts
sections.intro: Sheet ghosts built from ᗣ, plus faces shouting boo. The Pac-Man line puts the ghosts on the chase.

sections.label: Bats & Vampires
sections.intro: Bats spread their wings with /|\ or ⎛⎝ ⎠⎞. Vampires show teeth with 皿 or ▿ and often hold the trident ψ.

sections.label: Zombies
sections.intro: The ¬ is a stiff outstretched arm and º-° are mismatched eyes. Repeat the face for a horde.

sections.label: Pumpkins & Witches
sections.intro: Witches cast with a wand drawn as ━☆, and the spider face gets its legs from /╲/\ on each side. The spider uses Telugu letters for eyes, so a device without that font shows boxes.

sections.label: Scared
sections.intro: Reactions for a horror film, a jump scare or a dark hallway.

faq.q: Which character makes the ghost in Halloween text art?
faq.a: Usually ᗣ, U+15E3 from the Unified Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics block. Its dome and scalloped bottom edge look like a sheet ghost, which is why Pac-Man text art writes the chase as ᗧ···ᗣ.

faq.q: How do you type vampire fangs in a kaomoji?
faq.a: Unicode has no fang character. Kaomoji use 皿, whose vertical bars look like a row of teeth, as in (｀皿´)ψ, or a small downward triangle ▿ under the eyes. The 🩸 or 🦇 emoji beside the face makes the vampire reading obvious.
It is a zombie walking with one arm reaching forward. The ¬ is the stiff arm, and º and ° are eyes of different sizes. Typing it two or three times in a row makes a zombie horde.
